info.title: JalRakshak API
info.description: Prototype. All villages, people, assets, IDs and readings are fictional demo data. No government system is integrated.

post.description: Exchange username and password for a session token. Errors never say which of the two was wrong.

get.description: Complaint inbox for Gram Panchayat and officers, limited to the villages they are responsible for.
Serve a complaint photo only to its owner, or to GP/officers responsible for that village.

post.description: Reload the seed and delete uploaded photos, so the demo story can be run again. Demo mode only.
Accept a batch of readings from one node. The node proves who it is with its device key.

get.description: Recent readings for one sensor, oldest first (ready to chart).

Node health and the latest value of every sensor. 'offline' means the node stopped reporting:
an equipment problem, which must not be read as a water-supply problem.

Open alerts from the rules engine (scripted story alerts excluded). Re-evaluates first, so a node that
has gone silent is noticed even when no new readings arrive.
Live alerts raised in the last `minutes`, open or cleared, newest first.
The score in use, the data source of every factor, recorded-vs-live comparison and what-if checks.

post.description: Officers publish a new version of the scoring rules. It becomes active immediately; old versions stay.
Roll back (or forward) to an existing version.

get.description: Pipelines where the current evidence is worth an incident (MEDIUM or HIGH) and none is open yet.

post.description: Preview the fused evidence for a pipeline without creating anything.
The Gram Panchayat opens an incident from the current evidence. The system proposes; a person decides.

get.description: Restoration check for an incident. Judges any supply windows that ended since the last look.

post.description:
The Gram Panchayat closes a repaired incident without sensor proof (e.g. no sensor on the pipe).
It is recorded as "Resolved - not sensor-verified", never as verified.

get.description: The signed-in user's notifications, newest first (in-app only in the prototype).

post.description:
Move a task one step forward. Recording the repair also writes a repair record for the pipeline,
which feeds its risk score (prior failures) and its history.

get.description: Anomaly detection, disruption forecasts, the water-quality outlook and the failure outlook.
Estimated functionality of every household tap connection, by zone and village, from live readings.
Our village, service-area and scheme IDs next to the national (mock) IDs they are keyed on.

post.description: Run every mock connector once, now. Nothing is sent outside this server.

get.description: Points with their latest verdict, the recent tests, and the status of every zone (Gram Panchayat and officers).
The status of one zone. A villager gets their own zone; no measurements are shown, only the verdict and date.

post.description: A trained tester's field-test-kit result. Judged on the server; a failed tap test raises an alert and a boil-water advisory.

get.description: Alerts for the user's villages, most urgent first. Re-evaluates first, so the feed is current.

post.description: Record that someone has seen an alert. It stays open until its condition clears; acknowledging twice changes nothing.

get.description: Pipelines ranked for preventive attention. Officers see all their villages, the Gram Panchayat its own.

post.description: Plan a preventive inspection: opens a PREVENTIVE incident from the planner's reasons and its task, in one step.

Today's service validation for the villager's own household: did water come, how much, how did it look.
A second submission the same day replaces the first.

get.description: The villager's own tap: its status, how it was decided, and the zone's water-quality screen result.
Household taps in the zones the user oversees, worst first. Filter by zone or status.
Indicators for one slice of the hierarchy and for each unit directly below it (the drill-down).
State > district > block > village for the villages the user can see (to build a drill-down tree).
Villages as GeoJSON points (RFC 7946) with their current indicators, for any GIS tool. Positions are fictional.
Open-format exports of what the user may see. No names, phone numbers, complaint text or photos are included.
Who did what, when: every write is recorded. Officers only. Free text and photos are never stored in it.
Deployment facts an administrator needs: database, data volumes, retention and which safeguards are on.
Everything the current frontend needs in one call (seed shape plus server-computed risk).
Pipelines ranked by inspection priority. The score is explainable and is not a failure probability.

complaint_codes.title: Complaint Codes
complaint_codes.description: Leave out to use all unassigned reports in the area

Channel.title: Channel
Channel.description:
How the villager reported. Missed-call (IVR) and WhatsApp let people without a smartphone app report;
in the prototype those channels are simulated in the app and post here as the signed-in villager.

note.title: Note
note.description: Why the rules are changing (kept in the audit trail)

date.title: Date
date.description: Defaults to today; cannot be in the future

ts.title: Ts
ts.description: When the readings were taken; defaults to arrival time

note.title: Note
note.description: Why the incident is closed without sensor verification

quantity.description: ENOUGH or LOW when water came; leave out when it did not

failure_type.description: Required when the repair is recorded
